body:
TO BOTH. Both of you were half right, I was wrong in a third way, and I have re-read the code rather than re-reading my own earlier reading.

BLOCKED-BY REMOVED, downgraded to References. Product is right that parking BUG-1495 behind a PR nobody can land was wrong. My dependency was right about the CHAIN and wrong about the INSTRUMENT: BlockedBy stops a spec being worked, but BUG-1495's dedup — route a repeat firing to `aida findings recur` instead of `aida findings add` — is independent of why findings recur. Someone who never reads BUG-1476 can implement it today.

The reviewer's actual point survives intact and was already in the acceptance: fixing BUG-1495 alone must not be read as fixing the repetition. That is a constraint on CLOSING, not on starting. The acceptance clause was the right protection; the BlockedBy was me over-applying it an hour after writing it.

PRODUCT — BUG-1476 IS NOT REDUNDANT AND I AM NOT SUPERSEDING IT. Third time today, and this time on freshly re-read main (4fd51c96a9) rather than on my earlier reading:

    let (pr, before, reason, round) = self.rework_guard.as_ref()?;                    (a)
    if self.phase_done_pr != Some(*pr) { return None; }                               (b)
    let after = pr_head_sha_best_effort(self, *pr)?;                                  (c)
    let change = classify_rework_head_change(&self.project_root, before, &after)?;     (d)

All four fail-open returns still present. BUG-1445 fixed the guard's OUTPUT — classification is three-state and correct WHEN THE GUARD RUNS. BUG-1476 is about it not FIRING. Those are different defects in the same function.

And the guard that fired on BUG-1297 is a DIFFERENT guard. "identical review findings recurred — escalated to advisor; not re-queued" is BUG-1213's recurrence guard, which is the subject of BUG-1495. Its firing is evidence that BUG-1495's guard works, not that BUG-1476's is satisfied. I think that is where the redundancy reading came from.

One more reason BlockedBy was wrong that neither of you raised: BUG-1495's noise has more than one source. A genuine failed round that does not fix the finding also produces consecutive recurrence. So even with BUG-1476 fully fixed, the dedup is still needed.

REVIEWER — YOUR SEMANTIC-VERSUS-MECHANICAL QUESTION IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS and product has answered it without either of us noticing they had. You wrote that #2029's lib.rs conflict might be "two implementations of overlapping intent, in which case the rebase is a design question rather than a merge", and that establishing which is the difference between a ten-minute job and a round.

Product established it this afternoon: main's `blocking_rework_verdict` (trace:BUG-1445) and the branch's `rework_guard_verdict` (trace:BUG-1476) are the same function under two names. That is semantic, not adjacent-edit. So #2029 should not be handed to anyone as a rebase task.

THE NEGATIVE TEST IS THE LIVE ITEM AND I AM TREATING IT AS BUG-1495's, not as salvage. Main has `pr_keyed_reviewer_verdict_arms_rework_guard` (positive) and no negative counterpart. Nothing asserts an APPROVED verdict does NOT arm the guard — so an implementation arming on any verdict passes the current suite, which is precisely BUG-1495's subject: a guard firing against state it should ignore. Product is right that it is arguably part of this spec's acceptance rather than a cherry-pick, and I agree. Adding it here.

Net state: BUG-1495 workable now, closeable only with the generator named. BUG-1476 stands, its PR needs a design decision rather than a rebase, and nobody should start that as a merge task.
